selection.tie_rule: first model in the stated fixed candidate order; exact score ties only
selection.selection_uses: validation patient-macro MAE averaged over SBP/DBP and three seeds only

observed_test_evidence.abstract_latex: Separately, SE-last has primary-test SBP/DBP MAE 12.386/8.002 mmHg; SE-minus-CNN changes are SBP -0.20 [-0.48, +0.07]; DBP -0.36 [-0.53, -0.18] mmHg (descriptive paired 95\% patient intervals). Across the six required three-seed models, the lowest observed primary-test MAEs are SBP 12.386 mmHg for SE-last and DBP 8.002 mmHg for SE-last. These observed test comparisons do not change validation-based selection.
observed_test_evidence.discussion_latex: Across the six required three-seed models, the lowest observed primary-test MAEs are SBP 12.386 mmHg for SE-last and DBP 8.002 mmHg for SE-last. These are descriptive endpoint-wise minima among prespecified fitted models, not a new model-selection rule or evidence of global superiority. Capacity and placement controls retain their distinct roles; supplementary ECA and single-seed sensor ablations do not enter this six-model summary. For SBP, SE-last minus CNN is -0.199 [-0.480, +0.068] mmHg. SE-last's observed SBP MAE is lower than CNN's (change -0.199 mmHg); its paired interval includes or touches zero. For DBP, SE-last minus CNN is -0.359 [-0.534, -0.184] mmHg. SE-last's observed DBP MAE is lower than CNN's (change -0.359 mmHg); its paired interval is wholly below zero. All intervals compare a fixed model with CNN, not the lowest model with every competitor; they are descriptive, conditional on the fitted seeds, and not adjusted for multiple comparisons or selecting an observed minimum. An interval including zero leaves the direction uncertain without erasing the observed point estimate. A validation-selected model need not have the lowest test error, and a lower observed test error is not a deployment-selection decision.
